why: A is hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic ∧ proposition_5_35 ∧ admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert (the last at universe 0). A ⇒ B is proved using A, and the derivation has two parts. First, proposition_5_35 applies to B's Hilbert E₀ (‖v‖² = b(v, v); B's symmetry of b is unused) and gives the pointwise bump property f(x) ≠ 0, which implies B's literal one (f not identically zero on O, with U = O ∩ W). Second, admitsBumpFunctions_of_hilbert gives AdmitsBumpFunctions, hence AdmitsBumpFunctionsWeak. Its hypothesis is a chart around each point with Hilbert E₀, which B's equivalent atlas of sc-Hilbert charts supplies (level 0 only, IsChart via MAtlas.equiv_iff). B ⇒ A fails for real reasons, not lack of effort. (1) A concludes the pointwise notions (HasBumpProperty, AdmitsBumpFunctions), while B gives only the not-identically-zero ones, and on retracts weak bumps do not give pointwise ones by glue. (2) hasBumpProperty_of_quadratic needs only κ‖v‖² ≤ b(v, v) for a continuous bilinear b: a Hilbertable E₀, with b not even symmetric. B covers only an E₀ whose given norm is Hilbert.
overlap: n/a (B_to_A not proved). A_to_B uses only AdmitsBumpFunctions.weak and MAtlas.equiv_iff besides the hypothesis.
